sections.content:
Blob3 is selected at (18,35), target ring at (18,23) — the cell where blob2 used to be! g pixels: (18,24-25), (19,23-26), (20,23-26), (21,24-25) → center (19.5,24.5) = cell (18,23). So blob3's target = (18,23).
Interesting! Blob3's target is exactly the position where blob2 was. And blob2's target was (18,11), which was… to the left of blob1's original position (18,17). Blob1's target is (18,29) — the position to the right of blob2's original position (18,23).
So the targets form a chain: blob1 (18,17)→(18,29); blob2 (18,23)→(18,11); blob3 (18,35)→(18,23).
Hypothesis: the targets are a permutation — each blob's target is another blob's original position (or an empty cell). This looks like a "swap/rotation" puzzle: the blobs have to move to their designated cells.
Predicted pattern: blob4 (24,41) → target is somewhere; blob5 (36,41) → target is somewhere.
If the targets form a cycle: for example blob1→(18,29)?? But (18,29) was originally empty. Hmm.
Original positions: P1=(18,17), P2=(18,23), P3=(18,35), P4=(24,41), P5=(36,41).
Known targets: T1=(18,29), T2=(18,11), T3=(18,23)=P2.
Hmm, T3 = P2. Maybe T1 = P3? No, P3=(18,35) ≠ (18,29). T1=(18,29) is originally empty.
Maybe the targets are just fixed cells. Let me check the targets of blob4 and blob5.
Note: currently blob1 is at (18,29) = T1. Blob3 is at (18,35), target is (18,23) — the path (18,35)→(18,23) passes through (18,29) where blob1 is now! If I jump blob3 to (18,23), it will pass over blob1 → blob1 gets erased!
So order matters: I should jump blob3 to (18,23) before moving blob1 to (18,29). But blob1 has already moved to (18,29). Damn.
Wait, but maybe blob1 at (18,29) is "done" (it's on its target). Does a blob on its target still get erased when jumped over? Unknown.
Let me first check the targets of blob4 and blob5. Deselect blob3? Clicking another blob switches the selection (that's what happened in frame 4: clicking blob2 deselected blob1).
Let me select blob4 (24,41) → click (25,42).

<parameter=code>

res = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':25,'col':42}])
prev = previous_frame.ascii.split('\n')
cur = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
diffs=[(r,c,prev[r][c],cur[r][c]) for r in range(64) for c in range(64) if prev[r][c]!=cur[r][c]]
# find g ring center
gc=[(r,c) for r,c,a,b in diffs if b=='g']
if gc:
    rs=[a for a,b in gc]; cs=[b for a,b in gc]
    print("g ring bbox rows",min(rs),max(rs),"cols",min(cs),max(cs))
print("other diffs:", [(r,c,a,b) for r,c,a,b in diffs if b!='g' and a!='G' and b!='G'])
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
